answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so a seat is grown slow like a grove, never handed out free. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations, each spark gone in a gale. The toll climbs with head count like a thread pulled longer and longer, so cheap mass registration stalls against compounding compute.
